title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) that measured how often LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals would produce unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action, or unsafe‑execution rate) and whether a preregistered guarded pipeline (validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human‑gate) reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (as actually run: deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a shared single generation—see Disclosure) yielded baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). Conservative preregistered sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe (N=300, 28 both‑failed pairs) gives guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. We archive full execution, scoring, and validator artifacts (per‑episode JSON, provider traces, and SHA‑256 hashes). A documented, artifact‑backed deviation occurred: the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed; therefore the run does not evaluate the preregistered ensemble. All results, handling of failures, and provenance are reported exactly as archived.

sections.introduction: Modern agentic NetOps pipelines attempt to convert natural‑language intent into configuration changes that may be executed automatically. This raises a concrete operational risk: a plausible LLM text claim can become a real action (a configuration change) with side effects—what we term the claim→action (unsafe‑execution) problem. Prior work recommends generate–validate–repair patterns, multimodel consensus, and human gating as mitigations for text→action risk; however, empirical measurements with preregistered designs and full provenance remain rare. We therefore preregistered a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) to quantify: RQ — what is the absolute paired difference in safe outcome rates between an unguarded baseline and a preregistered guarded pipeline in a deterministic NetOps simulator? We emphasize two commitments: (i) preregistration of design and analyses before observation; and (ii) archival of all raw model calls, validator traces, scoring artifacts, and SHA‑256 hashes to enable exact reproducibility. Principal contributions: (1) a preregistered, artifact‑backed paired measurement; (2) transparent reporting of an execution deviation from the preregistration (consensus ensemble not executed) and conservative sensitivity accounting for failed calls; (3) release of per‑episode validator traces and an execution manifest so every reported numeric value is traceable to stored artifacts.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers examine LLMs and agents for NetOps, generate–validate–repair architectures, and verifier‑assisted tool use. Empirical claims→action pipelines were proposed and measured in related domains; taxonomies of agentic failure modes motivate conservative mitigations. Rather than reimplementing those systems, this study uses a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a hosted LLM to produce an operational, preregistered measurement with full provenance; all literature entries used for motivation and closest prior work are archived in the evidence bundle and cited in the references list.
sections.methodology: Preregistration: The plan (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26; preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) fixed the research question, paired design, N=300 tasks (100 benign / 100 ambiguous / 100 adversarial), inclusion/exclusion, validator, analysis procedures, and sensitivity rules. Key preregistered elements: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact McNemar two‑sided on paired binary outcomes; paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for the absolute difference; preregistered guarded pipeline = validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human‑gate. Execution: autonomous pipeline generated tasks (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), made hosted model calls (declared model gpt-5-mini per execution/model_configuration.json), parsed responses, ran deterministic_netops_validator_v5 to simulate effect and produce a binary safe/unsafe outcome, and archived all artifacts (execution/*, execution/scoring/*.json, execution/responses/*.txt). Retry and missingness policy: one automatic retry per failed call; pairs with incomplete outcomes were excluded from the primary complete‑pair analysis; preregistered sensitivity treated failed episodes as unsafe. Archival provenance: execution/execution_manifest.json contains full per‑file SHA‑256 hashes, provider call audits, and stage_counts. Analysis: contingency (n11,n10,n01,n00) on complete pairs; absolute paired difference, bootstrap CI, and exact McNemar p‑value reported. All analysis code executed against archived artifacts; analysis artifacts and hashes are in analysis/*.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.
sections.results: Execution and provenance (artifact values): planned episodes 600; completed episodes 544; failed episodes 56; model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28; stage_counts recorded (execution/execution_manifest.json) include {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}. These provider‑call counts and the per‑file SHA‑256s show a single shared generation per task and no executed multimodel consensus ensemble (see Disclosure). Primary analysis used 272 complete pairs (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Observed complete‑pair contingency: n11 = 271, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (N=272). Safe rates on complete pairs: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Missingness sensitivity (preregistered 'failure_as_unsafe'): include 28 both‑failed pairs as unsafe → N=300; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Representative scoring and validator traces (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json) are archived and contain the exact JSON fields used to compute reported numbers; per‑file SHA‑256s are in execution/execution_manifest.json. All numeric values in this section are derived from those artifacts.
sections.discussion: Main scientific interpretation (artifact grounded). The executed guarded condition in this run must be interpreted as the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a shared single generation; the preregistered multimodel consensus stage was not executed (execution manifest and provider_call audit show single shared_initial_generation per task). Consequently, any preregistered hypothesis that required the consensus ensemble (H2) was untested by this execution; we document that deviation and avoid ensemble claims. On the analyzable complete pairs (N=272) the observed absolute improvement is numerically very small (~0.37 percentage points) and statistically inconclusive (McNemar p = 1.0), with a bootstrap CI that includes zero but is bounded above at ≈1.10 percentage point. The run produced a high baseline safe rate on the analyzable pairs (≈99.6%), leaving little headroom for detecting small absolute improvements; the reduced analyzable sample (272 vs preregistered 300) lowered confirmatory sensitivity below the preregistered target. Provider/model call failures (28 pairs excluded) materially reduced effective N; execution/execution_manifest.json and the provider_calls/* traces record error counts and per‑call outcomes. Operational implication: in this deterministic simulator a validator applied to a single shared generation produced near‑perfect safety on the completed pairs, but we cannot generalize this to the preregistered consensus ensemble or to production devices. Reproducibility and next steps: all artifacts and per‑episode JSON traces (execution/scoring/*.json, execution/responses/*.txt, execution/execution_manifest.json) and analysis files are archived with SHA‑256s; researchers may re‑run the preregistered consensus ensemble on identical task seeds, fix provider failure causes, and evaluate ensemble effects. Limitations and threats to validity are enumerated below.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and ran a paired study measuring LLM→action safety in a deterministic NetOps simulator and archived complete execution and scoring provenance. On the 272 analyzable pairs the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared single generation) produced a trivial absolute improvement in safe outcomes (~0.0037) that is inferentially inconclusive; conservative inclusion of 28 failed pairs yields a comparable tiny absolute effect (~0.00333). A documented, artifact‑backed deviation prevented testing the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble; that deviation and the observed provider failures materially limit confirmatory claims. We therefore publish exact execution and scoring artifacts (SHA‑256 hashes recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json) and recommend re‑execution of the preregistered consensus ensemble with improved call reliability and larger, higher‑fidelity task banks to reach stronger operational conclusions.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track).
- Declared hosted model used in execution artifacts: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini").
- Orchestration/adapter used: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json).
- Deterministic validator used for scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/*.json include validator_id and validator_version = "deterministic_netops_validator_v5").
- Exact initial master prompt (immutable archived reference): provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. This immutable path+SHA‑256 is the required disclosure reference to the initial master prompt.
- Preregistration: hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design with N=300 and a guarded defense consisting of a deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human‑gate.
- What actually executed (artifact evidence): execution/execution_manifest.json records planned episodes 600, completed episodes 544, failed episodes 56, model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28, and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}. Provider call audit fields show condition_counts {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}. Per‑episode response and scoring JSONs (execution/responses/*.txt and execution/scoring/*.json) and their SHA‑256 hashes are archived and referenced in the execution manifest. These artifacts demonstrate that the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed; the guarded condition in the archived run corresponded to the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a shared single generation. The preregistered consensus hypothesis was therefore not tested by this execution.
- Tools and capabilities permitted and used: deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5), hosted LLM provider (declared gpt-5-mini), deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and an isolated deterministic simulator used by the validator. All per‑call provider traces and validator traces were archived under execution/provider_calls/* and execution/scoring/*.json and are included in the full hash manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Preregistration freeze and autonomy boundary: The preregistration was locked before observation (SHA‑256 above). After the autonomy lock the system autonomously generated tasks, executed model calls, validated configurations, scored outcomes, analyzed results, and drafted the manuscript; per‑step artifacts and hashes are archived. No human manual editing of technical content, numeric results, validator traces, figures, captions, references, or the Disclosure Statement occurred after the autonomy lock.
- Deviations and technical failures: A substantive, artifact‑backed deviation occurred: the preregistered consensus ensemble stage was not executed; this is recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json and provider_call audits (stage_counts and condition_counts). Provider/model call failures produced 56 failed episodes (28 task pairs) that were excluded from the primary complete‑pair analysis; this is recorded in analysis/missingness_summary.csv and execution/execution_log.jsonl. The preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') was applied and reported. All deviations, failures, and handling rules are archived and described in the manuscript.
- Human role: The human Research Director selected the topic family and approved the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock. After the lock all research formulation, execution, analysis, and manuscript text were generated autonomously; the provenance artifacts above document the autonomy boundary.
- Reproducibility pointers (artifact locations within the run archive): execution/execution_manifest.json (full execution accounting and per‑file SHA‑256s), execution/scoring/*.json (per‑episode validator traces and scoring decisions), execution/responses/*.txt (raw responses), analysis/* (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv, paired_difference_figure.svg), execution/model_configuration.json, and provenance/master_prompt.txt (initial master prompt reference SHA‑256 above).
limitations: Single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for production devices and long‑horizon workflows.

The preregistered multimodel consensus stage was not executed in this run (execution manifest stage_counts: {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}; provider_call audit condition_counts show {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}). The executed guarded condition therefore functioned as the deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate on a shared generation; ensemble effects cannot be inferred from these results.

Missingness: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were logged; the preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') is reported but failed calls reduce effective sample size and limit inference about small absolute effects.
High baseline safe rate on complete pairs (~99.6%) leaves little headroom for detecting small absolute improvements; interpret small observed differences cautiously.
